sample_description:
IMPORTANT - READ BEFORE PREDICTING. The stimulus texts of this study are not in the public data deposit; each arm below is therefore DESCRIBED from the study's own design codebook (format, number of reported effects, which statements were appended, approximate length) rather than reproduced. You are predicting from a description of the text, not from the text.

2,256 German adults who completed the survey (of 2,451 who started), recruited from a general-population online access panel and quota-sampled on gender x age band (18-44 / 45+) x school-leaving track (Hauptschule / Realschule / Abitur), with a screener requiring at least moderate self-reported interest in psychological research; fielded 2022 by the Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID). Not a probability sample. Arm sizes are listed separately below. Each respondent was randomised to ONE of 18 text formats and then read TWO German research summaries in that format, one after the other: first a summary of a meta-analysis on action video games and visual perception, then a summary of a meta-analysis on psychotherapy for depression. Immediately after each text they rated the researchers who wrote the reviewed meta-analysis on the 14-item Muenster Epistemic Trustworthiness Inventory (7-point bipolar adjective pairs), rated whether the results of the review are credible (1-8), and answered items on readability, understanding, feeling able to discuss the topic, topic relevance, epistemic emotions and four factual knowledge questions. Median completion time about 21 minutes.

message_texts_note: The German stimuli (18 formats x 2 topics) are NOT in the PsychArchives deposit. Each entry is a DESCRIPTION assembled from the codebook's value labels for the five s_iv_* design factors (20221202_ESM_Codebook.csv), the codebook's Bedingung labels, and the per-arm word counts hard-coded in the authors' R output (20230921_ESM_R_Output.html). Flagged inside every text and in sample_description.

provenance.verified_by: this adapter was verified host-side on 2026-08-25 by loading through ssb.task (see status); data/kerwer2025/README.md documents the vendoring agent's independent checks (arm table, METI subscale composition, quota-cell decoding from the R log)
readme_claims: N = 2,451 started, 2,256 completed (dispcode 31/32, dropout FALSE); 18 arms with analysis n 113-138
Bedingung maps one-to-one onto the five s_iv_* factor columns; incomplete factorial with arm 1 as the PLS core
METI subscales pls_METI_{Exp,Int,Ben}_k are the deposit's own composites of the 14 items (6/4/4), verified to 1e-9 by the vendoring agent
quota_assignment 1-12 decodes to gender x age band x school track via the mapvalues() call in the authors' R output
provenance.control_choice: Arm 1 (plain-language summary, 4 effects, no statements) is the reference cell of the incomplete factorial: 13 of the 17 other arms differ from it in exactly one design factor (arms 5, 6 add two statements; arms 15 and 17 differ in both format and effect count). The paper's H1 contrast (PLS vs abstract) is recoverable as the arm-16 cell versus control; H3 (COI statement) as arms 10 and 13 versus control.
caveats: THE STIMULI ARE NOT IN THE DEPOSIT. The brief carries codebook-derived DESCRIPTIONS of each format, stated inside every arm text. Treat like kim2024: a weaker brief than tasks with verbatim texts
German general-population quota sample screened on interest in psychological research (>= 4 of 8), fielded 2022; not a US sample, not probability-based, no weights
the trust object is 'the researchers whose meta-analysis I just read a summary of', not scientists in general; stimuli are long (159-699 words) research summaries, not short persuasive messages
all outcomes are 1-7 / 1-8 Likert or semantic-differential composites, not 0-100 sliders; METI means sit near 5.6 of 7 (ceiling-ish)

the *_psychotherapy outcomes come from the SECOND text read by the same respondents in the same arm: same randomisation, but a different topic and possibly order effects; the videogames block is the clean between-subject read, the psychotherapy block is not an independent replication
the three METI subscales are disjoint parts of one 14-item battery (item-total r >= 0.85), so their cells are not independent tests
design factors are not fully crossed; contrasts other than arm-vs-arm-1 are not encoded here
no respondent-level demographics beyond the reconstructed quota cell; the gender decoding follows the authors' own mapvalues() labels (G m/w) in the R log and is not in the codebook
